item.title: Ireland overcome Fiji to build up head of steam for South Africa clash
item.description: Ireland warmed up for a showdown with world champions South Africa by labouring to a 43-15 Nations Championship victory over Fiji in Dublin. The hosts had won all six previous Test matches between the sides but struggled for fluency and briefly trailed during an uncomfortable opening period at a subdued Aviva Stadium. Robert Baloucoune scored twice in the first half for Andy Farrell’s men after quick-fire tries from Fiji pair Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato overturned Tommy O’Brien’s early opener. Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter, O’Brien and Nick Timoney went over in the second half as Ireland eventually pulled clear to keep alive their hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final. The result leaves Ireland level on 20 points with second-placed England in the northern hemisphere standings – a point below leaders France – ahead of next week’s mouthwatering clash with the Springboks. Head coach Farrell made seven personnel changes and two positional switches to his starting XV following last week’s convincing 42-12 win over Argentina, but insisted the selection was not experimental. Wing O’Brien, one of those recalled, crossed wide on the left to give Ireland an eighth-minute lead. Robert Baloucoune ran in two tries during the first half (Brian Lawless/PA) However, the hosts’ early promise faded after Jamison Gibson-Park had a try ruled out on review due to a knock-on. Fiji centre Tuisova powered over following a line-out maul before Jiuta Wainiqolo burst through a weak Irish defence to tee up captain Yato to put the visitors ahead. Boos rang around the ground when referee Angus Gardner ruled Ireland number eight Timoney had been held up on the line. Baloucoune then crossed twice in quick succession on the right, either side of a disallowed try for Fiji prop Luke Tagi, to restore order. Ronan Kelleher kickstarted Ireland’s second-half scoring (Brian Lawless/PA) But Ireland ended an underwhelming opening period with a slender 17-15 lead as Fiji fly-half Ben Volavola slotted a penalty after home captain Tadhg Beirne was sin-binned. Hooker Kelleher dived over at the start of the second half before O’Brien had to be alert to deny Volavola a breakaway try after he had charged down Sam Prendergast’s attempted clearance. Pop star Niall Horan was among the Lansdowne Road crowd and the scrappy contest gradually started to go in one direction. Nick Timoney wrapped up the victory for Ireland (Brian Lawless/PA) James McNabney’s Ireland debut from the bench lasted a matter of minutes after he was flattened by a swinging arm which resulted in a yellow card for Fiji’s replacement prop Inoke Ravuiwasa. Loosehead prop Porter bulldozed over following that incident before wing O’Brien’s 10th try in as many Tests increased the home side’s advantage further. Timoney completed the scoring by stretching for the line late on, but Ireland have work to do if they are to upset South Africa in seven days’ time.

item.title: From travel troubles to turf shoes, Tulane overcomes unusual obstacles at Rice
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 24: Makai Williams #42 of the Tulane Green Wave, Zach Dresch #47 of the Tulane Green Wave and Cayden Dees #58 of the Tulane Green Wave run on the field prior to a game against the UTSA Roadrunners at Yulman Stadium on October 24, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Playing on the road in college football is challenging enough. But for several programs in Week 11 of the 2026 season, getting to the stadium became a battle of its own. On Friday, Nov. 13, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop, disrupting air travel across the country. The stoppage was just the third nationwide ground stop of the 21st century, following the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks and a Jan. 11, 2023 system outage. The Tulane Green Wave were preparing to fly to Houston for their matchup against Rice when their travel plans came to an abrupt halt. With no clear timeline when flights would resume, Tulane pivoted to an alternative that wasn’t a feasible option for many other programs affected by the shutdown. The Green Wave decided to take a nearly six-hour bus ride to Houston. “I want to give a big shoutout to (Chief of Staff) Chris Hatcher and (Director of Football Operations) Rory Thornton,” Tulane head coach Will Hall said. “When we got stopped right there on the tarmac, the efficiency with which they were able to turn this thing around — also credit to our administration, David Harris our athletic director, Patrick Norton, Justin Schemmel, and everybody involved right there to make sure this team was taken care of the best it could.” Tulane’s busses stopped in Lake Charles for a driver change before continuing west on the six-hour trek. The Green Wave ultimately arrived at its Houston hotel past 2 a.m. on Saturday. During the early stages of the trip, Rice and the American Conference agreed to delay the kickoff time two-and-a-half hours, pushing it from 1 p.m. CT to 3:30 p.m. CT. “We ended up bussing over,” Hall said. “We had our normal hotel meetings at the facility. We ate at the facility, we bussed over, we got here about 2:30 in the morning. And thank the league and thank Rice for backing up the kick time a little bit to allow our guys to sleep a little longer. It wasn’t an easy turn of events, but it’s what we want. We know that hard times develop hard men and tough times develop tough men. That’s what we tell our young men, and I thought they handled it elitely. They didn’t in any way use it as an excuse. We knew we had to win this game together. We knew it was gonna take all three phases, and we did it.” Roughly 13 hours after arriving in Houston, Tulane kicked off at First Community Stadium. The Green Wave withstood a sluggish start and turned a 17-6 halftime deficit into a 20-17 victory. A second half shutout from the defense and a late offensive surge allowed the team to secure its second consecutive road win over Hall after a night of complicated travel. “

item.title: '£47m? Why not?' - Former Liverpool centre-back Dejan Lovren tells club to seal bargain permanent deal for Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo
item.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Liverpool defender Dejan Lovren has urged the Reds to trigger their €55 million (£47m) purchase option for Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo. The 27-year-old centre-back has quickly become a mainstay at Anfield since arriving on a season-long deal from the Catalan giants in August. Uruguayan defender impresses on loan Lovren believes Anfield chiefs should waste no time tying down Araujo beyond June 30, 2027 following his seamless transition to English football. Since completing his temporary switch in the summer, the Uruguay international has featured in all 10 of the Merseysiders' opening Premier League matches, starting eight of them. His parent club still hold the defender under contract at Camp Nou until June 2031 . Former centre-back praises physical attributes Having registered 185 appearances and eight goals across all competitions during a six-year spell on Merseyside between 2014 and 2020 before departing for Russian outfit Zenit Saint Petersburg, the Croatian knows what is required at the heart of the backline. Across his English top-flight career, he tallied 162 outings and seven goals - combining 31 games and two strikes at former club Southampton with 131 matches and five goals for the Reds. Speaking to Tribal Football , Lovren explained why the newcomer thrives in England: "I believe the Premier League suits Ronald Araujo more than the Spanish league. Because he is a physically dominant guy, it suits him perfectly. "I believe he will only improve and, I don't know, maybe in the future he can agree to stay permanently. In the Premier League, Liverpool won't be his only option, but Liverpool are smart enough to consider their options, he's quite young at 27. So why not keep him if he's doing so well?" Purchase clause offers bargain value With rival top-flight clubs likely to monitor the centre-half's availability if he returns to Spain next summer, the former Croatia international feels the reported buyout fee represents an opportunity too good for his old employers to ignore. Pressing the hierarchy to make the arrangement permanent, Lovren added: "£47m? Why not? In the near future, he will probably cost £80m, so why not take him at this price and make him an even bigger and better player along the way? He's at a perfect age. He has a good five to six years at the top football level to play. So why not?" Fierce rivals visit Anfield next Addressing his long-term plans recently, Araujo insisted it remains "too early" to decide where he will play his football next season. For now, the defender is focused on helping fourth-placed Liverpool build on their 18-point haul from their opening 10 league outings. Once the international break concludes, the Reds return to top-flight action at Anfield against fierce rivals Manchester United in Matchday 11 on Sunday, November 22.

item.title: 'I still need to improve defensively!' – France surprise package Lucas Da Cunha opens up on Zinedine Zidane's tactical shift
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-FRA-TRAINING - AFP France midfielder Lucas Da Cunha has admitted he still needs to improve his defensive work after being deployed in a holding role by Zinedine Zidane. The Como captain discussed his rapid international rise ahead of Les Bleus' crucial UEFA Nations League fixture against Turkey. Lucas Da Cunha embraces surprising France role Como captain Lucas Da Cunha has quickly established himself as a surprise revelation under France coach Zinedine Zidane. Installed in a deep defensive midfield role, the 25-year-old has caught the eye during Les Bleus' UEFA Nations League campaign. Following a narrow defeat to Italy, Zidane's side are gearing up to face Turkey in Bordeaux. Da Cunha is expected to feature heavily as France look to secure qualification. Adapting to a demanding defensive midfield position Traditionally deployed further forward at club level under Cesc Fabregas, Da Cunha admitted that anchoring the French midfield requires a completely different physical and tactical approach . "It's true that I have a different role at Como, where I play further forward. Here, I'm in front of the defense, I don't have to push forward as much as at club level, but I like both positions," Da Cunha explained. "This holding midfield role is new to me; it requires a lot of defensive work, and physically I'm not a monster. I have to win back possession, and I can still improve defensively." Cesc Fabregas and Zinedine Zidane's influence Da Cunha credited his development at club level under Fabregas with preparing him for the tactical demands of international football. Since moving to Italy, the former Rennes youngster has successfully transformed from a winger into a complete central midfielder. The Como skipper also highlighted the personal support he received from Zidane after receiving his maiden senior call-up in September. "He made me feel that I wasn't there for nothing, he talked to me a lot to get to know me, our relationship is very good," Da Cunha revealed. Speaking about captain Kylian Mbappe ahead of the Turkey clash, the midfielder added: "He's in good form and we can feel he's fully committed to us. Like all of us, he's confident before the match." Preparing for high-stakes clash against Turkey France enter Sunday evening's encounter at the Stade Atlantique knowing that victory is essential to bounce back from their San Siro setback and secure quarter-final qualification. While Zidane remains calm following their first defeat in charge, insisting that the squad is entirely focused and not worried, the pressure is on Les Bleus to deliver. With Da Cunha anchoring the midfield and Mbappe leading the attack, France are primed to finish their group stage campaign on a high note.

item.title: “He Should Never Play Another Game for USC”: Trojans Fans Sick of Jayden Maiava After 3 INT Performance in 27–13 Loss vs. Indiana
item.description: Southern California Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava. © IMAGN USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava had a disappointing outing in the 27-13 loss against the Indiana Hoosiers. He threw three interceptions, including two in the fourth quarter that helped No. 9 Indiana secure the victory. Maiava completed 26 of 42 passes for 311 yards and one touchdown. In the three losses USC has suffered this season, Maiava has thrown for 894 yards with four TDs against six interceptions, struggling in tougher matchups. Fans shared their opinions on Maiava after USC’s loss against Indiana. “Jayden Maiava should never play another game for USC,” one fan wrote. USC QB Jayden Maiava Accepts His Mistakes in Indiana Loss Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava started well in the first half against Indiana, completing 14 of 16 passes for 145 yards, one touchdown and one interception. The game was tied at 10 entering halftime. However, Maiava struggled in the second half. With USC trailing 20-13 in the fourth quarter, linebacker Isaiah Jones picked off Maiava inside Indiana’s five-yard line. Maiava was then intercepted by Jamari Sharpe in the fourth quarter to end any comeback hopes for USC. His first interception came in the second quarter to Indiana defensive back Preston Zachman, setting up a 21-yard field goal for the Hoosiers. After the loss, Maiava acknowledged he could have done better. “Just got to play better at the quarterback position. Trust it and be able to flush it,” Maiava said via SI . “It was a great defense. We got a really great offense as well. Just got to play better at the quarterback position.” The defeat is USC’s third of the season, denting its chances for a spot in the 12-team College Football Playoff field. item.title: England are favourites against All Blacks, and fearless Wales are an inspiration
item.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick's side's emphatic 78-15 thrashing of Japan and looks ahead to the match against New Zealand next weekend. I would love to see the England players absolutely bombarded with the favourites tag before their meeting with New Zealand next week. Perhaps even over-egg it a little bit - I want to see how this side handles it. At the end of the day, beating New Zealand or South Africa will likely be a requirement if you want to win a Rugby World Cup. Are England really favourites? Yes, I genuinely believe they are. While victories over Australia and Japan have been encouraging, it was Wales' epic win over the All Blacks on Saturday that has given me real faith that this England side is good enough to compete at the highest level. The key question is whether they can play as they have done over the last two weeks while carrying the favourites tag. England are playing a better style of rugby than New Zealand. I thought the All Blacks' attack, particularly in the second half in Cardiff, was incredibly one-dimensional. That is nothing for England to be afraid of as their own attack has been very slick this campaign. New Zealand aren't going to fix those issues in a week, and England should be capable of soaking up that style of attack defensively. Of course, the All Blacks were missing some frontline players, including Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie, Will Jordan and Jordie Barrett. However, what I saw during the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series was the Springboks beginning to work out that style of play after losing the first Test. They went on to win the next three Tests in a row. Two Tests to turn England into World Cup contenders Having beaten the All Blacks last year, I don't want England to approach this home fixture with an underdog mentality. This side needs to get used to being a contender. The next few weeks could prove crucial in determining whether they are genuine challengers at next year's World Cup. An undefeated autumn, regardless of whether they finish top of the northern hemisphere standings in the Nations Championship, would elevate England to contenders for the Six Nations. Two weeks ago, England would have been delighted to find themselves in this position. Now, the reward could be two massive Tests against the very best. They are not at the level of France or South Africa yet. I think those two sides, particularly after Friday's Test match, are still a little bit ahead of everybody else. However, England have a good chance of facing New Zealand back-to-back over the next two weeks. What an unbelievable opportunity that would be and what a feather in the cap it would represent for this team. It would not only give the players belief in what they are capable of achieving, but also send a message to the rest of the world that they can beat New Zealand and potentially follow that up with another victory over the All Blacks or South Africa. item.title: 3 takeaways from No. 2 Utah’s thrilling victory over No. 23 Arizona
item.description: Arizona wide receiver Isaiah Mizell (17) leaps for a first down against Utah in the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Tucson, Ariz. | Rick Scuteri, Associated Press In a game that saw seven lead changes throughout, the No. 2 Utah Utes overcame a delayed flight, an almost entirely unavailable Wayshawn Parker and a slow start to down Noah Fifita and the No. 23 Arizona Wildcats in an absolute thriller, 40-39 on the road Saturday. The Utes trailed 14-3 before scoring the game’s next 14 points to go up 17-14. From there, the teams went back and forth, exchanging leads as they both showcased their offensive explosiveness led by their respective quarterbacks. Here are three keys that led to Utah’s win. Utah played just well enough to overcome three turnovers A week ago against BYU, the Utes created havoc for rival quarterback Bear Bachmeier as he threw four interceptions, two of which were thrown from inside the 10 when the Cougars were close to scoring. This week it was the other way around. Devon Dampier had a poor pitch that did not find his running back’s hands, and after falling to the ground, found the arms of an Arizona lineman ready to pounce on the first play of the second half, one that Arizona also capitalized on for six points. Dampier also threw an interception in the third quarter that was picked by Arizona’s Jay’Vion Cole at the 1-yard line, where Fifita put together a 99-yard drive to retake the lead. Utah punt returner Mana Carvalho also muffed a punt that gave the ball right back to Arizona. However, the Ute defense held strong for a three-and-out to escape the situation with just giving up a field goal. Ultimately, despite costly mistakes, Dampier’s 204 passing yards and 100 rushing yards were enough to get the job done with assistance from Daniel Bray in the backfield. As the Utes have seen, momentum swings can be the difference in losing and winning. Fortunately for the Utes Saturday, the turnovers did not cost them the game, but head coach Morgan Scalley will surely make ball security a point of emphasis in the week ahead as the Utes look to the TCU Horned Frogs. item.title: Dana White admits he was wrong about Josh Hokit after UFC 334: 'Stock went up with me'
item.description: Josh Hokit may not have won Saturday night at UFC 334, but he still delivered a memorable performance in his first UFC main event . Heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane successfully defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Hokit at New York’s Madison Square Garden, a bout that earned Fight of the Night honors and a $100,000 performance bonus for each man. Although the result marked Hokit's first career defeat in 11 pro fights, UFC CEO Dana White couldn't have been more impressed with the outspoken contender. "It was an incredible fight," White said backstage at the UFC 334 post-fight press conference. "The pace he set was insane, and I think it was freaking everybody out — this smaller guy, the way he was just coming at [Gane]. But even if you look at the significant strikes, they were doubling every round. The total punch stats were massive, too. "If you see the score of the fight, they had it two-to-two going into the last round. I didn't see it that way, but it doesn't tell the story of the fight either. You have to see the fight to believe it." Hokit, 28, has experienced a meteoric rise since joining the promotion a year ago. In that time, White has openly admitted a distaste for how the former NFL player has presented himself with his character work and controversial comments, most notably when Hokit insulted former First Lady Michelle Obama on the White House’s South Lawn . Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit had an all-out war of attrition Saturday at UFC 334. Caleb Bowlin via Getty Images White said he even scored Saturday’s fight four rounds to one in favor of Gane — yet he still believes the fight went perfectly for Hokit, despite a loss being the official result. "What he did was he went in there, and if you really think about going into this fight: How does Josh Hokit win this fight?" White said. "Ciryl Gane moves like a middleweight. He turned it into a street fight from the second the bell rang in the first round. Literally, he didn't win, but he fought the perfect fight. What other way could he possibly fight Ciryl Gane than the way that he did? "My thing was, after the first round, holy s*** — if he can keep this pace for five rounds, Gane's in big trouble. Too big, carries too much muscle and blah, blah, blah. But actually, Gane looked his best in the fourth and fifth rounds. "There's no doubt that Hokit's stock goes up. Even with me," White continued. "I thought this guy was a big-mouth goofball and I hated his schtick and the whole thing. I respect the s*** out of that guy [now]. He is the real deal. Stock went up with me." Hokit beat two longtime heavyweight contenders, Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis , to earn his title shot. The latter came on the big stage that was UFC Freedom 250 at the White House in June. item.title: 'Of course it is annoying!' – Zinedine Zidane blasts media reports over his relationship with Kylian Mbappe
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-FRA-TRAINING - AFP France head coach Zinedine Zidane has strongly denied any friction between himself and captain Kylian Mbappe. Speaking ahead of their crucial UEFA Nations League fixture against Turkey, Zidane branded media speculation regarding their relationship as entirely false and annoying. Zidane hits back at Mbappe rift rumours France head coach Zinedine Zidane has firmly put to bed any talk of a strained relationship with national team captain Kylian Mbappe. Speaking ahead of Sunday's crucial UEFA Nations League clash against Turkey in Bordeaux, Zidane addressed media speculation head-on . With Les Bleus needing a victory to secure qualification on a high note, the manager stressed that unity within the camp remains absolute. 'The relationship is perfectly fine' Press conference inquiries quickly turned to rumoured friction between the manager and his star striker ahead of the Stade Atlantique fixture. With an impassive expression, Zidane made it clear that stories of a fallout are completely wide of the mark. "I don't quite understand what's being written," Zidane stated firmly. "I'm not going to get into the debate; the relationship is perfect. For the player as well as for me. I can't stop what's being said." When pressed on whether the ongoing reports had frustrated him, the former midfielder admitted that the speculation is wearing thin. "Yes, the things that come back to me, of course, are quite annoying," he added. Tactical plans and squad updates for Turkey On the pitch, Zidane confirmed that Mbappe will start in his preferred position, leading a 4-3-3 attacking trident as France look to bounce back from a 3-1 defeat against Italy. "Of course it changes everything, we'd rather have him with us than not have him," Zidane noted regarding his talisman. Elsewhere in camp, young forward Désiré Doué trained despite struggling with an unstable tooth following an elbow from Davide Frattesi. Meanwhile, players like Michael Olise and Bradley Barcola are tipped to support Mbappe in attack, with defensive changes expected as Les Bleus chase victory. All eyes on Bordeaux showdown with Turkey Sunday evening's encounter at the Stade Atlantique carries massive significance as Les Bleus aim to bounce back and seal their qualification status in style. Zidane's men know that a strong performance against the Turks will banish memories of their San Siro setback. With the squad fully focused and their captain primed to lead the line, France are ready to deliver a statement display in their final group outing.

item.title: “Tennessee Broke This Man’s Soul”: Fans React to Mike Elko “Begging for His Job” With His “Utter Apology” After Texas A&M’s Loss
item.description: Texas A&M Aggies head coach Mike Elko during warm ups before Auburn Tigers take on Texas A&M Aggies at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Ala., on Saturday, Nov. 23, 2024. Mike Elko has not been a name that many will hear about this season, but he made himself known on Saturday – for the wrong reasons. Shortly after Texas A&M suffered a 7-22 home drubbing against Tennessee, the Aggies’ head coach opened his post-game presser with this statement: “Utter apology with everything that I have to everybody that supports this program. Thank you for turning out; you deserve so much better. Give me a chance & we will get this fixed and put a much better product on the field.” His attempt at contrition, unfortunately, was met with derision and condemnation from fans: The game was notable for some underwhelming quarterback performances. For Texas A&M, Marcel Reed completed only nine of 22 attempts for 71 yards and was intercepted once, while Brady Hart added another pick. The team’s only touchdown came on a KJ Edwards run. George MacIntyre, meanwhile, had just 109 yards for Tennessee before exiting in the third quarter with a knee injury, but he set up two field goals for Cooper Ranvier. After taking over, Faizon Brandon threw a touchdown pass to DeSaahn Brame and then set up three more field goals. Texas A&M HC Mike Elko discusses Aggies’ offensive woes vs. Tennessee All told, Mike Elko had just one word to describe how Texas A&M’s offense fared on Saturday: “Pathetic.” He continued: “The wind played a big role,” explained Elko. “The (pass) rush played a bigger role. Our inability to give (Marcel Reed) any time to see anything — they’re very multiple on defense — so the pressure created a massive challenge trying to do anything.” The Aggies will visit Oklahoma next week. Kickoff is at 11 a.m. CT. item.title: Coco Gauff’s Ex-Coach Urges Aryna Sabalenka to Make Major Changes To Her Team After WTA Finals Heartbreak: “Hard Questions to Figure Out”
item.description: Aug 8, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, Canada; Aryna Sabalenka reacts after missing a point against Ekaterina Alexandrova (not pictured) during the fourth round at the National Bank Open at Sobeys Stadium. © John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Coco Gauff’s former coach Brad Gilbert weighed in on Aryna Sabalenka’s WTA Finals disappointment, urging the Belarusian to make changes to her coaching team. The Belarusian stopped working with Max Mirnyi ahead of the WTA Finals, but is still working with head coach Anton Dubrov and performance coach Jason Stacy. Sabalenka’s run at the WTA Finals ended after she lost two of her three round-robin matches. She failed to win a Grand Slam this season and did not lift a title since the Sunshine Double. Sabalenka was also surpassed by Elena Rybakina for the top spot in the world rankings. Noting Sabalenka’s lackluster run, Gilbert suggested she make changes to her team. He opined that if he were in Sabalenka’s place, he would have promoted Mirnyi as head coach. On the Big T podcast , Gilbert also suggested that she make changes to her serve and forehand. “I think the biggest thing for this off-season is going to be the serve, and I do feel all of a sudden the forehand, which I do think is her best shot, has been letting her down a lot. I think she might need some changes to her team. I heard she let Max Mirnyi go. I would have promoted him to head coach. She’s got some hard questions to figure out this off-season to start the year very positively because she’s played well Down Under (at the Australian Open) the last few years.” Sabalenka has won the Australian Open twice, in 2023 and 2024. Aryna Sabalenka apologizes after video of her comments to fans spreads online Aryna Sabalenka issued an apology after a video of her comments to fans surfaced online after her WTA Finals loss to Elina Svitolina. “I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online. My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment. That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.” Screenshot of Aryna Sabalenka’s Instagram story. Elina Svitolina, meanwhile, advanced to the final of the year-end event, where she will take on Mirra Andreeva. item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin Answers Tough Question About $91 Million Investment in Him
item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers looks on during the first half of an NCAA football game against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan Hare Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) Getty BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 14: Head Coach Lane Kiffin of the Louisiana State Tigers and Head Coach Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns interact on the field after the game at Tiger Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) Getty The LSU Tigers spent big money when they went out and got Lane Kiffin. A first-year home run was never guaranteed, and building something new can involve trial and error regardless of the coach’s experience. Still, LSU wants results now, and a 6-4 record made a question about its investment entirely fair. After Saturday’s 22-21 loss to Texas, Kiffin faced that question during his postgame media session. The Tigers committed to a seven-year, $91 million contract when they hired him. Asked about the expectations surrounding his arrival, Kiffin gave an answer that started where it needed to: with accountability. “Fair question, and I get it,” Kiffin said in footage of the news conference provided by Mike Scarborough of TigerBait. “Underperformance.” Lane Kiffin Acknowledges LSU Needs More Wins That opening was the strongest part of his response. Kiffin did not dismiss the premise or suggest that close losses should satisfy people who expected more. He acknowledged the gap between what LSU hired him to do and what the Tigers have delivered. “It doesn’t matter if the game’s been close or they go down to the last whatever, six seconds,” Kiffin said. “I’m brought here to win, and we need to win more than that.” The Texas game made that point particularly painful. item.title: Manchester City Eyeing £35 Million-Rated Lens Goalkeeper Amid Gianluigi Donnarumma Struggles
item.description: Manchester City Eyeing £35 Million-Rated Lens Goalkeeper Amid Gianluigi Donnarumma Struggles Gianluigi Donnarumma has struggled in net for Manchester City of late. More Videos Gianluigi Donnarumma remains Enzo Maresca’s first-choice goalkeeper, but it has not been the most convincing start to the season for the Italian. A number of costly errors have placed his form under scrutiny, forcing Maresca to publicly back his No. 1 on more than one occasion and prompting some supporters to argue that their side needs more competition between the sticks. With Geronimo Rulli approaching 35 years of age, that competition would likely have to come from the transfer market - which is where a new name linked with Manchester City will raise eyebrows. It’s safe to assume that the club’s recruitment staff have continued to track the next generation of goalkeepers across Europe even after the signing of Donnarumma, and fresh rumours suggest the search has taken them to France. Trophy-winning Lens shotstopper being considered by Man City The name in question is RC Lens goalkeeper Robin Risser, who was part of France’s World Cup squad in the summer after a meteoric rise in senior football. According to Swiss outlet 4-4-2.ch , as relayed by Sports Mole , Manchester City are leading the chase for the 21-year-old and are considering an opening bid of around £26 million ahead of the summer window. Lens, however, are holding out for at least £35 million for a player contracted until June 2030. Risser was central to a superb 2025-26 campaign at Lens as they finished second in Ligue 1 and lifted the Coupe de France. That form earned him the UNFP Goalkeeper of the Year award and a place in the competition’s Team of the Year. The 6ft 4in Risser boasts a commanding aerial presence and composure on the ball, making him exactly the kind of profile that would suit Manchester City ’s build-up play. The sticking point is a sell-on clause inserted by Strasbourg, reported as 25 per cent of the total fee - or 25 per cent of the profit according to L’Équipe - meaning a significant chunk of any sale would be owed to his old club. Risser’s current season has admittedly been more difficult than the last, not least with a chastening 9-1 UEFA Champions League defeat at home to Como earlier this month. His standing at international level has held firm, though, with the youngster called up under both Didier Deschamps and new France boss Zinedine Zidane. That promise has not gone unnoticed elsewhere. Liverpool and Manchester United are reportedly both keeping tabs, as are Serie A pair Inter Milan and Juventus, while Newcastle United and Tottenham have shown interest in the past. No formal offers have been tabled as yet.

item.title: Dominik Livakovic talks life in Barcelona, training and game-time under Flick
item.description: Dominik Livakovic talks life in Barcelona, training and game-time under Flick Dominik Livakovic was somewhat of a surprise signing for Barcelona when the club roped him in the summer for a fee of just €2 million. It was an investment made keeping in mind Wojciech Szczesny’s future, with Livakovic immediately being promoted as the main alternative to Joan Garcia. Currently on duty with the Croatian national team, Livakovic has opened up about his time at Barcelona so far, including his lack of game-time among other things. Livakovic on game-time at Barcelona Livakovic has won 84 caps for Croatia. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Livakovic was asked whether or not his lack of minutes at Barcelona affects his standing in the Croatian national team. “I play for Barcelona. I’m just a young man from Zadar, and I’m very proud of that. I’ve already kept goal for this great club. I train and wait for my chance, and I feel like I’m in good shape,” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). Livakovic, who started in the recent game against England , went on to describe the training process at Barcelona, which he labelled tough. The goalkeeper added that he is waiting for his chance to impress. “Training at Barcelona really is very tough, because we’re talking about the best players in the world. It would be ideal to play in goal in every match, but I’m waiting patiently for my chance ,” he added. Livakovic has so far made only one appearance for Barcelona since joining the club in the summer. That lone appearance came against Sevilla earlier in the campaign. Livakovic on being awarded Fiery Heart trophy Livakovic is regarded highly in Croatian football. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Meanwhile, it was a special day for Livakovic as he was awarded the Fiery Heart trophy for his selfless service to the Croatian national team. Speaking about the accolade, the goalkeeper said, “This award has made me very happy, because it comes from the fans who give football its passion and special emotions. “ “I truly care, from the bottom of my heart, about the national team’s success, and I’m happy that the fans recognized that and appreciated it in this way. “ Livakovic added that it’s an honour to follow in the footsteps of Croatian legends such as Ivan Perisic and Luka Modric, previous recipients of the award. “It’s wonderful to follow in the footsteps of Luka and Perišić, who won this award before me, and that alone shows its value. “I thank everyone who took part in the voting, and I extend a special thank-you to all the fans who continue to support us, whether things are going well or we’re going through tougher times,” he concluded.

(Photo by Frederick M. Brown/Getty Images) Getty Former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills head coach Rex Ryan was in the news for the wrong reasons this week. After stepping away from coaching in 2016, Ryan joined ESPN as an NFL analyst, primarily appearing on “Sunday NFL Countdown.” However, he turned himself in to Nashville authorities early Wednesday morning after allegedly running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck on Broadway Street. Ryan drove away but eventually stopped at a red light, where he got out and argued with the pedestrians. He then returned to his vehicle and left the scene. Authorities later identified his license plate and traced the truck’s registration to him. The former NFL coach now faces six misdemeanor counts: leaving the scene of an accident (2), failure to give information or render aid (2), and failure to obey a traffic control signal (2). Will Ryan Be on ESPN Sunday Morning? With Sunday morning approaching, a big question is whether Ryan will appear alongside the NFL Countdown crew, which consists of host Mike Greenberg, Alex Smith, Teddy Bruschi, Randy Moss and Adam Schefter. As of now, according to a statement from an ESPN spokesperson, Ryan will be on the show, and there is no expectation that he’ll address the matter. “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.” Ryan also usually appears on the morning show “Get Up” on Mondays following the NFL slate, so it’s likely he’ll be on air for each of the next two days. item.title: Notre Dame has already started its college football playoff run
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; South Bend, Indiana, USA; Notre Dame Fighting Irish cornerback Christian Gray (29) celebrates a stop against the Boston College Eagles during the second half at Notre Dame Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Michael Caterina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Notre Dame Fighting Irish probably play more playoff football than anyone in the country. That statement isn’t a brag, it’s just the reality Notre Dame has been living for the last three seasons — and it’s mostly their own fault. In 2024, Notre Dame lost to Northern Illinois in the second game of the season, and they played win or go home football all the way to the National Championship game against Ohio State. In 2025, Notre Dame lost two very close games to start the season, and then went on to pound the rest of their 10 opponents until the playoff committees executed the PROTECT ALABAMA GAMEPLAN, and left the Irish stranded in South Bend. 2026 is very much the same as both 2024 and 2025. After the loss to BYU, there was no room for error for the Irish — especially when they were initially ranked No. 11 in the first CFP rankings as opposed to their No. 4 AP Top 25 ranking. The Miami game (because who really cares about the Navy game) was the first playoff game of 2026 for the Irish. They don’t get the special treatment that everyone believes they do — that alone is for the circle jerking of the SEC (obviously). After Notre Dame’s win over Miami, a few of the talking heads in the media tried selling people the idea that even if the Irish do drop one of their last three games — they’re still probably IN the playoffs. The unproven truth, however, is that those statements are FALSE and misleading as hell. The bigger discourse going on right now isn’t about which teams are getting into the CFP, it’s about which conferences get what number in the playoff. All Notre Dame has to do is slip, and this committee will be ready to push them off of a cliff. All of THAT is why Notre Dame’s 41-7 win over Boston College is fairly encouraging. The Irish were coming off of a huge win, and on a gloomy and cold day, they went out there and beat the hell out of a crappy team. I know that doesn’t sound exciting, but it shows how locked in this Notre Dame team is right now. The Irish went out there and put up 500 yards of offense, and gave up just 136 yards. Jonaz Walton, alone, outgained the entire Boston College team. Notre Dame has two games left of the regular season — which is basically just a couple of “play in” games. None of it has to be pretty, as an 11-1 Irish team who is currently ranked No. 5 in the CFP rankings is a lock to get in the thing. Still, as it is with any playoff run, Notre Dame has to be absolutely locked in to the task at hand. In doing that, Notre Dame should win these games by a good margin — and then it’s onto round two of the playoffs (which is actually round one or a bye week).

item.title: Should the Bruins Keep 30-Goal Pace Forward Or Sell High?
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 12: Casey Mittelstadt #11 of the Boston Bruins looks on during the first period against the Montréal Canadiens at TD Garden on November 12, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty Casey Mittelstadt has seven goals in 20 games. That puts him on roughly a 30-goal pace over 84 games. When GM Don Sweeney traded Charlie Coyle for Will Zellers, a second-round pick, and a top-six winger who has suddenly become second in goals behind the Bruins’ David Pastrnak, it looked like a pretty good deal. But beneath the surface, this hot start might lead the Bruins to make a key decision. Should the Bruins Sell High? Middelstadt had a solid run with the Buffalo Sabres. As a member of the Bruins, his early 2026-27 run has become better than good. He noted, “Being in the same spot for a couple years now, I feel very comfortable here. I think it maybe takes me a little bit more time than normal people. So yeah, I think that’s been huge for me too.” Now that he’s gotten more comfortable, should the Bruins double down and hope he’s a key part of their future or move on while he looks appealing to the rest of the league? Mittelstadt is scoring at a 25 percent clip. He has seven goals on 28 shots. But his shooting average is only around 13 percent, and over an 84-game stretch, this elite percentage is likely to regress. He has good skill, and he’s fitting in. But he might not be the kind of player the Bruins should sign to a big contract, even though he’s off to a very hot start this season. The reality is that both Mittelstadt and Pavel Zacha, who makes $4.75 million, are in contract seasons. Mittelstadt makes $5.75 million, and both will become UFAs. What do they do? If Mittelstadt finishes near 30 goals, he won’t settle for a small raise. He’ll ask for $7 million or more on the market. The core question now is whether they should pay free-agent prices for a 28-year-old winger whose numbers might be inflated this season because of his high shooting percentage. The Bruins Have Players Ready for the Next Step The deal is that giving Middelstadt a bigger contract might slow the development of some of Boston’s younger players. James Hagens is out for a few weeks on IR with a back injury, but he’s already shown he can be a top-six player, perhaps on the second line. There are also a number of other players in the next wave, including Matt Poitras, Dean Letourneau, who’s playing with Boston College and doing really well, and Will Zellers, the prospect the Bruins got in the trade involving Coyle. Perhaps there are two good choices here. If Mittelstadt proves to be solid all season long and has a career season, keep him. But you don’t want to put him in the way of other youngsters who are coming up through the ranks. He could be a trade bargain . Or he could just be the kind of player you keep around and see what he does. If Boston has a legitimate playoff team, why would you move somebody who’s so productive?

This is the level England will have to reach to win Euro 2028 , as both Rice and Thomas Tuchel expounded on. Except, for all the grandeur that the midfielder described, Uefa have lessened the stakes. In the first two iterations of the Nations League , this game at the Metropolitano would not just be a game to win the group but a direct qualification play-off. Only the first-placed teams went through. The rematch of Spain v England promises to be interesting but has less jeopardy than it should (Getty) And sure, it might not be the World Cup or the Euros, but the very prospect of elimination from a competition that does at least mean something would have naturally made this fixture more compelling. As it is, with both teams secure in the top two well ahead of Croatia and Czech Republic, there’s a question over whether they will even play their best sides. None of this is to say the game won’t be as enjoyable as the brilliant September meeting , it’s just that it’s not what it could have been. And that fits with a needless trend in football right now. The current game apparently has an obsession with safety nets – something to catch the endless bloat. Everything that could have expanded has expanded. The expansion of the Nations League has taken the edge off today’s game (Getty Images) Uefa themselves started this with the Euros. In 2016, a total of 16 teams became 24, with 16 also going through to the knockout stages. The clean binary symmetry of the old two-from-four groups was gone. item.title: Why This Bulls Center Is a Top Trade Target for Warriors
item.description: The Golden State Warriors are off to a strong start this season with an 8-5 record, but they’ve lost two straight, and an injury to Steph Curry , who was playing at an All-NBA level, has already set them back. The Warriors have gotten strong contributions from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg , who is averaging 20.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 3.5 assists. His play has helped offset the loss of Kristaps Porzingis, who was dealing with health issues and announced that he would be stepping away from basketball for the time being. The team could be looking elsewhere to help out in the frontcourt, as they are reportedly interested in Jalen Smith of the Chicago Bulls. NBA Insider Jake Fischer said on “Deals and Dunks” on SiriusXM NBA Radio that the Warriors have contacted the Bulls about Smith and strongly indicated that the Warriors are interested in Smith. He said that Smith was someone “high on Golden State’s list.” Smith was drafted tenth overall in 2020 by the Phoenix Suns. He was signed by the Bulls in the 2024 offseason. He is averaging 13 points, 7.8 rebounds, and two assists this season while shooting 51% from the field and 34% from three. He is in the final year of his deal, making $9 million this season before becoming an unrestricted free agent in the offseason. Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Can The Warriors Get A Deal Done And Should They? The Warriors are reportedly looking to trade Porzingis and his $20 million contract, but they would need to attach draft compensation since Porzingis is unlikely to play this year, if ever again. The Warriors likely have no problem attaching some second-round picks to get Smith, but would they be willing to move off a first for a player who may only be there for one season? They have their own first from now until 2032, and if they are confident in their playoff positioning and Smith’s value, a deal could get done. The Bulls are continuing to rebuild, and though Smith has been good for them this season, he’s not a long-term player for them as an upcoming unrestricted free agent who is behind Nic Claxton and Caleb Wilson on the frontcourt depth chart. Otherwise, Golden State would have to deal some combination of Will Richard, Gary Payton, and De’Anthony Melton to make the money work. Payton and Melton can’t be traded until December 15. If the Warriors can get a deal done for Smith, they should take the swing. Draymond Green is logging minutes at the center position right now, as Al Horford is 40 and can’t play the heavy minutes he used to, and Porzingis is absent. Draymond at the five used to be the Warriors’ way of decimating teams, but those days are long gone and Draymond at the five is now an undersized option without the infrastructure and offense to carry things.
